ledger.note: 926: the county first appears as a vassal state of France. Infobox: 'Vassal state of France, 926–1477', earliest count 'First count mentioned ?-926' with no name. The page gives no origin story; Abbeville is the chief town. [Reviewer eu-10-x, 2026-10-25] counterpart changed from kingdom-of-france (dossier 987-1792) to west-franks (843-989), the kingdom in 926.

1279: Eleanor of Castile, wife of Edward I, inherits Ponthieu, which passes to the English crown. 'In 1279 Eleanor of Castile, wife of King Edward I of England, inherited the County of Ponthieu'; her son Edward II later received it.
1294: Philip IV confiscates Ponthieu and the French crown holds it. 'However in 1294 Ponthieu was confiscated by King Philip IV of France.'
1303: Ponthieu reverts to the English crown after the Gascon War. Page: it 'reverted to Edward after the Gascon War (1294–1303)'; the page gives no separate year, so the war's end year is used.

1360: the Treaty of Brétigny puts Ponthieu under English control. Page: Brétigny 'gave control of Ponthieu (along with Gascony and Calais) over to the English' (Edward III had reached the region in late August 1346 before Crécy).
April 1369: Charles V of France conquers Ponthieu and the French crown holds it again. 'In April, 1369 Charles V of France conquered Ponthieu.'

20/21 September 1435: the Treaty of Arras gives Ponthieu to the Duke of Burgundy. The Arras page lists Ponthieu with the Somme towns, Auxerre, Boulogne and Vermandois as vassal domains of the Duke of Burgundy; the Ponthieu page: Charles VII won Burgundian support in exchange for 'possession of Ponthieu'.
1477: Louis XI reconquers Ponthieu from Burgundy and the county becomes crown land. 'In 1477 Ponthieu was reconquered by King Louis XI of France'; infobox 'Crown land of France, 1477–1836'.
1477: Ponthieu ceases to be a separate county and becomes crown land. Infobox: 'Crown land of France, 1477–1836'.

wars.name: Gascon War (Ponthieu)
wars.outcome: Philip IV confiscated Ponthieu in 1294; it reverted to Edward after the war (1294-1303).
wars.note: The Gascon War article itself was not opened; the Duchy of Aquitaine dossier (eu-10) carries the war.

certainty.note: A small county with no boundary record on the page; the 35 km disc round Abbeville is my reading.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from two pages (County of Ponthieu, Treaty of Arras 1435). The county page gives no area and no boundaries; it names Abbeville, Le Crotoy (fortress on the Somme mouth, built 1150, restored by Edward III, burned in 1372) and Crécy-en-Ponthieu.
SEQUENCE CONFLICT: the Crown lands page (royal-domain-of-france dossier) has 'Ponthieu conquered' in 1336 and 'given to England in 1360'; the Ponthieu page has Eleanor of Castile inheriting in 1279, Philip IV confiscating it in 1294, the English holding it again, Edward III reaching it in August 1346, Brétigny (1360) putting it under English control and Charles V conquering it in April 1369. The Ponthieu page has no 1336 or 1337 event. The royal-domain dossier draws the page-dated 1336, 1360, 1369, 1435 and 1477 changes of its own.
The state is the county itself and is drawn whole from 926 to 1476; its holders change (English crown 1279-1294 and 1303-1369, French crown 1294-1303 and 1369-1435, the Dukes of Burgundy 1435-1477) and each change is a rename event; the holders' own dossiers (royal-domain-of-france, burgundian-state, the Kingdom of England) carry the gains and losses of the land, so the compile should draw the county in the holder's colour or tint. Montreuil-sur-Mer, which the Crown lands page gives to the domain in 988, is not part of this county on the page.
